briefs.body: Turn the operator's paint statement into a written pass rule. Read tmp/freebuff/reports/paint-gunmetal-reference-plan.md (checks C1 to C5), Working/Q/PREDICTIONS_LOOKS.md rows Q1-2, and the paint rule inside tmp/freebuff/queue/9143-rc5-paint-channels.txt. Operator facts: the body is dark gunmetal satin with specular edges, darker carbon-weave inset panels, white chevron decals, rain beading; project policy is that BmAK fidelity wins and compromises are never offered as questions. Write Working/Appearance/ACCEPT_PAINT.md with one table: check id, what the frame must show, the numeric rule (relative to neighbouring panels where no absolute value exists), the member that moves it, and the fix-card owner file. State plainly that the combine rule is UNKNOWN and that C1 tests hue and edge contrast, not exact luminance. Mark which rules need the reference-luma file from the footage brief before they become absolute. Also list every sentence in 9143 that claims brighter JC3 lighting is accepted, with a note on where the operator said so. Done check: table has 5 rows plus a rain-beading row marked judged-by-JC3-weather, and the file cites each source path. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Collect measured reference numbers for the Batmobile body from footage the operator already recorded. Start from Research/BatmobileGrab/FOOTAGE.md and C:/Users/User/Videos/Captures (list the clips, open only files you can name). Use ffmpeg if present (PATH or Tools; if absent, say UNKNOWN and stop) to export single frames where the car is side-on in daylight, in shade and at night, into Working/Appearance/ref_frames/. For each frame sample three body panels (front wing, door, rear haunch) outside specular highlights, 200 pixels each, using a small python script Tools/scripts/ref_luma.py (--write, --check) and store mean sRGB, linear luma, and max-min over max. Write Working/Appearance/REF_LUMA.json and a coverage note listing which of noon, dusk, night, rain have no frame at all. Edit nothing else: promoting the hue rule of ACCEPT_PAINT.md from relative to absolute is a later job. Done check: JSON has at least 3 lighting conditions or an explicit missing list, and the script --check reprints the same numbers. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Run the five-minute experiment named in section 3.2 of tmp/freebuff/reports/paint-gunmetal-reference-plan.md. Find the grab TGA for Batmobile_V3_Body_Decals_D (Working/Appearance/grab; list in Research/BatmobileGrab/TEXTURES.md), convert it to a PNG under Working/Appearance/diag/ with an existing Tools/scripts texture reader, and look at it. Report with pixel evidence: does it hold white chevron shapes, on which alpha, at what pixel bounds; or is it noise or flat. Then read the 58 faces of slot 8 (Research/BatmobileGrab/SLOTS.md, MESHES.md) and say whether their UVs land on those shapes. Output Working/Appearance/DECAL_FINDING.md with a one-line verdict, either TEXTURE-BOUND-FIX or GEOMETRY-ONLY, the evidence image path, and the one owner file to edit. If the image cannot be opened write UNKNOWN with the failing step. Build nothing. Done check: verdict line present and the PNG exists with non-zero size. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Plan the darker carbon-weave inset panels. Inputs: section 3.1 of tmp/freebuff/reports/paint-gunmetal-reference-plan.md, Working/Appearance/build/coverage.md lines 420 to 445, tmp/freebuff/reports/app-microdetail-bake-plan.md, app-anisotropic-highlights.md, and the Carbon_Colour lines of Research/BatmobileGrab/SKINS.md. Question: which panels of the base body carry insets, what channel separates them (the PropertyMap t2 channel), and which JC3 CarPaintMM members can show a lower-luma tiling pattern there (second channel gloss, metallic, tint G or B, a weave baked into the albedo s1). Never answer that JC3 has no system; name the closest one and its gap. Write Working/Appearance/CARBON_PLAN.md with: inset regions by LOD0 slot, the exact members or bytes to edit, the expected luma ratio against the 75 percent rule of check C3, the bake source and size in KB, and the file that would settle each UNKNOWN. Done check: every inset region has a named carrier or an explicit missing-capability card. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Plan the satin finish with sharp specular lines on panel edges (check C2). Read the post-9032 body rows of Working/Translation/T_ROWS.jsonl (T-MA3, T-MA4), tmp/freebuff/reports/paint-plans-v2.md sections 1 and 2, app-reflectance-f0.md, app-anisotropic-highlights.md and the ClearCoat and GLOSS_CAP handling in Tools/scripts/factors.py. Decide with numbers which CarPaintMM values give a narrow bright highlight on a mid-gloss base: clearcoat level, base gloss, F0, and the aniso-ramp substitute. Show the arithmetic against the C2 rule (peak at least 1.6 times the adjacent diffuse luma, halving within one eighth of the panel width) and name the parts of that rule a number cannot predict. Output Working/Appearance/SATIN_PLAN.md: a table of member, current value, proposed value, source, risk, then an UNKNOWN list. Do not edit factors.py. Done check: every proposed value traces to a decoded BmAK parameter or is labelled a derived guess with the range to try. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Build the paint addendum on top of the RC5 paint branch. Read the report of 9143 (rc5-paint-channels.md) and the three plans Working/Appearance/DECAL_FINDING.md, CARBON_PLAN.md and SATIN_PLAN.md. Copy Builds/bm-RC5-paint to a new tree Builds/bm-RC5-paint2 (never edit the original). Apply in this order: equalised linear channels for hue (check C1), clearcoat and gloss values for edge response (C2), the inset channel split with the baked weave texture (C3), and the chevron route chosen by the decal finding (C4). Script Tools/scripts/rc5_paint2.py with --write and --check. Where a plan marks a value UNKNOWN keep the 9143 value and log it. Register the tree with a branch record under Working/RC5/branches/ in the format of the 9100 report. Added textures must stay inside the allowance of Working/Appearance/BUDGET_RC5.md when that file exists. Done check: --check prints each edited member read back from the built container beside its planned value, with zero mismatches beyond float tolerance. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Independent read-back of Builds/bm-RC5-paint2. Do not reuse the --check of Tools/scripts/rc5_paint2.py; open the built .ddsc and material containers with Tools/scripts/upk_read.py and the dds reader, and recompute from bytes: the three body channel values, the clearcoat and gloss floats, the inset channel assignment, the decal texture binding, and each texture's size against Tools/scripts/bm_budget.py. Predict check C1 by computing (max-min)/max of the final albedo in sRGB and the blue-versus-red order, and C3 by the luma ratio of inset to panel on the baked texture itself. Write Working/Appearance/PAINT2_VERIFY.md with measured against planned for every item and a PASS or FAIL line each. Each FAIL gets a one-variable fix card at Working/Appearance/fixcards/paint2-<n>.md naming file and member. Done check: the report lists at least 12 measured items, none taken from the build script's own printout. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Close the conflict between the rule that nothing is omitted and the 88 dropped components of Working/Appearance/APPEARANCE_PLAN.md. Read STAGES.md (closest-system rule), the dropped-class lists in tmp/freebuff/reports/appearance-drops-b.md and app-dropped-classes-plans-a.md, and the 9143 report. For each dropped class (mud, damage chapters, colour ramps, wetness, micro-detail, glass layers, editor scaffolding and the rest listed there) write a ledger row: class, closest JC3 system, the gap, the build action and the brief or file that carries it, or the sentence 'operator-signed no visual effect' with the operator fact it rests on (no visible damage stages, no scratches). Editor scaffolding classes may be called non-feature only with an evidence path. Output Working/Appearance/DROPPED_ROWS.md and DROPPED_ROWS.json. Done check: no class is marked drop without a reason, and the row total equals 88 or the file explains the difference. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Write the palette tints. Read Research/JC3Grab/TINT.md, TINT_WRITE.md (palette .vmodc layout: four float32 at Tint+20, stride 80), tmp/freebuff/reports/tint-palette-impact.md, paint-slots-palette-verify.md, and the T-MA7 row. Goal: all ten palette tints carry the body colour the paint branch decided (take it from Builds/bm-RC5-paint2 if it exists, else from 9143) and gloss 0.600, so any menu pick looks like BmAK. Create Builds/bm-RC5-palette with only the palette resource copied from the donor, edit the tint floats by byte offset, and keep the layout identical so a re-import is byte-stable. Script Tools/scripts/rc5_palette.py (--write, --check). Also record the CCar.palette hash the entity file points at and whether an entity edit is needed; if the path from palette to cb6 is still UNKNOWN, say so in the report and do not guess. Done check: 10 of 10 tints read back equal to the intended floats and the file size is unchanged. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Check Builds/bm-RC5-palette from the bytes. Parse the palette resource independently of Tools/scripts/rc5_palette.py, print all ten tint records with their offsets, compare them with the colour in Working/Appearance/ACCEPT_PAINT.md and the body block of the paint tree, and diff the container against the donor to prove only the intended floats changed. Also answer from files alone whether a tint replaces the baked albedo colour (use tmp/freebuff/reports/tint-palette-impact.md and Research/JC3Grab/TINT.md) and label the answer EVIDENCE or UNKNOWN. Write Working/Appearance/PALETTE_VERIFY.md. A tint that differs gets a fix card at Working/Appearance/fixcards/palette-<n>.md. Done check: the diff lists changed byte ranges only inside tint records, and the report ends in PASS or FAIL. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Fifteen body paint slots had no source in tmp/freebuff/reports/paint-slots-palette-verify.md (cb2, cb6, cb8 and the s0 half). The hook readout brief 7982 builds a live vehicle readout; read its report and the Tools/hook sources to see whether shader constant buffers or material parameter blocks of a spawned vehicle can be read. With that, plus Research/JC3Grab/CB0_SLOTS.md, UNIFORM_RECORDS.md and TINT_WRITE.md, rewrite the apply plan so each of the fifteen slots has one outcome: a source value with its file, a read recipe for the hook, or UNKNOWN with the single observation that would settle it. Output Working/Appearance/PAINT_SLOT_SOURCES.md and a JSON beside it. Do not run the game. Done check: 15 of 15 slots carry exactly one of the three outcomes, and each hook recipe names the hook source file and function to extend. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Reconcile the model and texture budgets across every RC5 branch. Figures in circulation: model 4,791.3 of 4,915 KB in Builds/bm-RC4/receipt.json step R9; texture 5,380.9 KB in Builds/bm-RC4-appearance/budget.json against a self-imposed 4,648 cap, 4,015.5 KB in tmp/freebuff/reports/build-d04-materials-textures.md, 5,855.8 of 7,065 in V-01-RC2; MODLOG.md lines 4100 to 4118 explain the cap. Run Tools/scripts/bm_budget.py on each RC5 branch tree built so far (booster, tracker launcher, lights, textures, paint2). Write Working/Appearance/BUDGET_RC5.md: one table of base plus per-branch KB, the hard walls, the self-cap and why it exists, remaining headroom, the silhouette margin (99.9004 against 99.9), and a trim plan for every branch that would overflow. Mark per-entity versus global budget UNKNOWN unless an evidence file says otherwise. Done check: one reconciled figure for each of the three disputed texture totals, with the arithmetic shown. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Derive or author substitutes for the eight texture rows with no pixel set: Micropattern A, A_N, B, C, Wheel_E, Body_ColourRamp, Underlayer_Ramp, Aniso_ramp. Read Working/Appearance/PIXEL_LOCATE.md and the 9054 report, Builds/bm-RC5-appearance from 9140, Builds/bm-RC4-appearance/texture_ledger.md, and tmp/freebuff/reports/app-microdetail-bake-plan.md, app-emissive-mask-channel.md, app-colour-ramp-textures.md. Per row choose one: derive from Batmobile_Microdetail, author the wheel-arch emissive strip from the four arch lamp geometries, bake a ramp into the albedo, or a stated neutral with the visible effect described. Create Builds/bm-RC5-substitutes, script Tools/scripts/rc5_substitutes.py (--write, --check), and stay inside the budget ledger allowance. Register a branch record under Working/RC5/branches/. Done check: 8 of 8 rows have a built texture or a written card naming the missing capability, and every built file is read back from the container. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Verify Builds/bm-RC5-substitutes without trusting the build script. Open each built texture with the dds reader: confirm format (BC1, BC3 or BC5 as intended), mip count, dimensions and byte size; compare the statistics (mean, min, max per channel) of each derived texture with its source in Working/Appearance/grab; for the authored wheel-arch strip, confirm the lit pixels fall inside the UV islands of the four arch lamp parts. Add the sizes to the total with Tools/scripts/bm_budget.py and print the headroom. Output Working/Appearance/SUBSTITUTES_VERIFY.md with PASS or FAIL per row and the new unfaithful count out of 23 rows (RC4 had 12). Failed rows get fix cards under Working/Appearance/fixcards/. Done check: the unfaithful count is stated with its row list and the rows sum to 23. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Decide and build the static state of the four chapter masks (Body, Weaponry, WheelArch, Undercarriage damage-chapter masks). Operator facts: no visible damage stages and no scratches; the car explodes at zero health. Read tmp/freebuff/reports/app-damage-chapter-masks.md, the 9140 report, Research/BatmobileGrab/MATERIALS.md for SupportDmgBlend, and the 9171 report. First settle from files which chapter state BmAK's playable Batmobile shows by default; if no file says, write UNKNOWN and choose the clean state the operator facts imply, with the reason. Then route that state through the closest carrier (SupportDmgBlend fixed at 0.0 with the mask baked into the albedo, a second slot, or vertex data) in Builds/bm-RC5-chapters with script Tools/scripts/rc5_chapters.py (--write, --check). Done check: all 4 mask rows leave the unfaithful list with a carrier named, and the read-back of SupportDmgBlend plus the baked textures matches the plan. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Bake the colour ramps into the surfaces they colour. Inputs: tmp/freebuff/reports/colour-ramp-in-material-members.md, app-colour-ramp-locate.md, app-colour-ramp-textures.md, and Builds/bm-RC4-appearance/texture_ledger.md (three ramp rows plus the Leather ramp, 64 by 512 pixels, whose sampler is absent from all 961 shader headers). The lookup rule lives in stripped material functions, so first write the rule you can evidence (which input drives the ramp V coordinate) and the parts you cannot as UNKNOWN. For the seat and body ramps choose the most defensible fixed ramp position with its evidence, sample that colour from the ramp, and bake it into the seat and body diffuse in Builds/bm-RC5-ramps (script Tools/scripts/rc5_ramps.py, --write and --check). Cockpit leather must read as dark leather, not plastic. Done check: 4 of 4 ramp rows have a baked result or a card, with the sampled RGB values printed beside the ramp coordinates used. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Review the first wave of appearance builds: paint addendum, palette write, absent-texture substitutes, chapter masks, ramp bakes, and the budget ledger. Re-read their reports and the verify files (Working/Appearance/PAINT2_VERIFY.md, PALETTE_VERIFY.md, SUBSTITUTES_VERIFY.md, BUDGET_RC5.md). For each, re-run its --check, recompute two values from bytes, and list every stand-in, guess or omitted row. Check that the combined texture additions fit the ledger headroom, that no branch edited a bm-RC4 tree, and that the 12 of 23 unfaithful count has fallen. If a fact changed (a value, file name, size or verdict), edit the text of later appearance briefs in tmp/freebuff/queue that have not started, and mark each edit with a line beginning 'Updated by review app-wave-1'. Done check: a table with one row per branch giving PASS, PASS-WITH-NOTES or FAIL, and the number of queue files edited. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Settle the canopy glass parameters one variable at a time. Read tmp/freebuff/reports/windscreen-and-glass-plan.md (sections 0 and 7), app-glass-layers.md, the Window block of Working/Appearance/build, and the 7982 hook readout report for any way to read material members. Decode the cb1 member order (SpecGloss, SpecFresnel, DiffuseRougness, PropertyMap t3) from the Research/JC3Grab shader notes, then list which BmAK glass scalar maps to which member, labelling the unproven ones. Operator fact: the interior is visible through the canopy and the screens glow. Build three probe variants of the Window block in Builds/bm-RC5-glassprobe/a, /b and /c, each differing from the baseline in exactly one member (tint opacity, then SpecFresnel, then alpha multiplier), with script Tools/scripts/rc5_glassprobe.py (--write, --check). Done check: each variant differs from the baseline in only the named member, proven by a binary diff printed in the report, and the decode table is complete. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Verify the glass probe trees offline. Diff each of Builds/bm-RC5-glassprobe/a, b and c against the baseline Window block bytes and print every differing offset; the rule is one member changed and nothing else. Parse each variant with the container reader used for the RC4 appearance tree to prove it loads, and confirm no texture was added (sizes unchanged under Tools/scripts/bm_budget.py). From the shader notes predict what each variant should do to the visible interior (more or less transparent, more or less reflective) and write the prediction as a numeric luma band for the interior region, plus the screen glow rule C5 (screen pixels at least 1.4 times the surrounding interior luma, blue at least red plus 20). Output Working/Appearance/GLASS_PROBE_VERIFY.md. Done check: 3 of 3 diffs show exactly one changed member and the prediction table has 3 rows. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Decode the channel packing of the cockpit specular texture Int_Cockpit_S, whose R channel is dead and whose packing is unknown, and cross-check the brake disc, missile and Nimbus S maps. Read tmp/freebuff/reports/app-per-pixel-reflectivity.md, the cockpit lines of Working/Appearance/build/coverage.md near line 60, and the cockpit materials in Research/BatmobileGrab/MATERIALS.md. Load each S texture from Working/Appearance/grab, print per-channel histograms, correlate the channels with the albedo and the normal of the same surface, and decide which channel carries reflectivity, gloss and metallic (or write UNKNOWN with the numbers). Compare with the JC3 CarPaintMM PropertyMap layout in Research/JC3Grab. Output Working/Appearance/COCKPIT_S_PACKING.md with a four-row table and the replacement mapping the banded substitute should use. No builds. Done check: each of the 4 textures has a channel table and a verdict DECODED, PARTIAL or UNKNOWN with the histogram file path. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Make the dashboard screens glow. Facts: the Int_Cockpit_E atlas was built but no CarLight block references it (texture_ledger.md R2), the emissive mask channel is not decoded (tmp/freebuff/reports/app-emissive-mask-channel.md), and the operator says the interior is visible through the canopy with screens glowing. Read app-cockpit-interior-materials.md, the candidate blocks listed in tmp/freebuff/reports/paint-gunmetal-reference-plan.md section 6 (slot 11 seat with EmissiveMultiply 15, slot 5 Emissive_Map, slot 12 Cockpit_Master_Flip_Data), and Working/Appearance/COCKPIT_S_PACKING.md. Decide which block shows the screens, bind the atlas to a CarLight block or the interior block, and set the emissive value so a night frame meets check C5. Tree Builds/bm-RC5-cockpit, script Tools/scripts/rc5_cockpit.py (--write, --check), inside the budget ledger. Done check: atlas binding and emissive value read back from the container, 0 unbound emissive textures remain, and the seat-versus-atlas decision is written with its evidence. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Verify Builds/bm-RC5-cockpit from bytes. List every material block that references Int_Cockpit_E or Wheel_E by texture index, print its emissive members, and prove the count of unbound emissive textures is zero. Check the atlas dimensions, format and size, the UV coverage of the screen quads in the interior mesh (lit pixels must sit inside the screen regions), and the total texture KB against the headroom in Working/Appearance/BUDGET_RC5.md. Compute the predicted night-frame contrast for check C5 (screen luma over surrounding interior luma, and the blue-minus-red margin) from the baked pixels. Output Working/Appearance/COCKPIT_VERIFY.md with PASS or FAIL per item; failed items get a fix card under Working/Appearance/fixcards/. Done check: the report lists the block names found, the unbound count, and the predicted C5 numbers. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Read back the lights branch Builds/bm-RC5-lights. For all 24 lamp rows list range, angle, falloff and the unit bridge used, and flag any value outside the shipped fleet domain (range 50, angle 50) that lacks a written reason; the RC4 values 60 and 70 are why the branch exists. For the 17 lens-flare entries print part and socket, and prove each socket exists on its part in the parts module. Compare headlight, tail and brake rows with the BmAK values in Research/BatmobileGrab/LIGHTS.json. Include the BmAK fact that underglow and arch lights are an emissive wheel material. Output Working/Appearance/LIGHTS_VERIFY.md as a table of rows with PASS or FAIL, plus a night prediction band for the later in-game take. Done check: 24 of 24 lamp rows and 17 of 17 flare entries appear in the table, each with a verdict. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Close the wheel and tyre gaps recorded in tmp/freebuff/reports/app-wheels-and-tyres.md and GRAB_BACKLOG.md line 1956. Items: front wheel lod2, lod4 and lod5 are unlisted in the wheel .lod; rim_radius 0.539 against the mesh leaves a 26 mm gap; the tyre UV layout is UNKNOWN (TYRES.md has none); brake disc glow; the four wheel lod4 and lod5 once unpacked (B-14). Use Builds/bm-RC5-parts from 9172 as the base, copy it to Builds/bm-RC5-wheels, and for each item either write the fix with its evidence or a card naming the file that would settle it. For the tyre UVs measure the tread island on the wheel mesh and write the result with the numbers. Script Tools/scripts/rc5_wheels.py (--write, --check). Wheel diameter is 1.366 m at true scale; keep it. Done check: 5 of 5 items closed or carded, rim radius and mesh radius printed from the built bytes with the gap in millimetres, and the model KB delta stated. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Verify Builds/bm-RC5-wheels from the built bytes. For each of the four wheels and each of the 5 LODs confirm the mesh is listed in the .lod, print the vertex radius against rim_radius and tyre radius (diameter must stay 1.366 m), confirm the brake disc material carries the emissive value planned, and count the faces per LOD against the BmAK counts in Research/BatmobileGrab/MESHES.md. Run Tools/scripts/bm_budget.py and print the model KB beside the headroom in Working/Appearance/BUDGET_RC5.md. Output Working/Appearance/WHEELS_VERIFY.md with a 4 by 5 grid of PASS or FAIL and the numbers behind each cell. Failures get fix cards in Working/Appearance/fixcards/wheels-<n>.md. Done check: the grid has 20 cells, none left blank, and the report states the final tyre-to-rim gap in millimetres. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

The Batmobile must never show damage. Operator facts: no damage stages and no scratches, and at zero health it explodes instantly. Read Research/JC3Grab/DAMAGE_MODEL.md, tmp/freebuff/reports/app-mud-and-dirt-default.md, the 9171 report, and the GRAB_BACKLOG.md APP-7 line, whose wording is stale. List every JC3 member that could still produce a damage look on this car (dirt and damage blend, low-health smoke, part detach, tyre burst visuals, deformation on the vehicle damage class) with its container, offset and current value. Build Builds/bm-RC5-nodeform with each of them set to the off value, script Tools/scripts/rc5_nodeform.py (--write, --check), and keep the 9171 explosion mechanism untouched. Rewrite the stale APP-7 wording in a new file Working/Appearance/APP7_REWORD.md (do not edit GRAB_BACKLOG.md). Done check: every listed member reads back at its off value, and the list names at least the deformation, dirt blend, smoke and detach switches or says UNKNOWN for each missing one. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Verify Builds/bm-RC5-nodeform and its interaction with the explosion branch. Read every member that app-26 claims to switch off straight from the built containers and compare with Research/JC3Grab/DAMAGE_MODEL.md; then diff the tree against the 9171 branch to prove the health-to-explosion rows are byte-identical. Search the whole RC5 merge inputs for any remaining damage-related nonzero value (deformation strength, damage mesh swap, burst) and list hits with path. Output Working/Appearance/NODEFORM_VERIFY.md with PASS or FAIL per member and a final list of residual risks that only a crash test can settle, each with the one observation for the later in-game take. Failures get fix cards in Working/Appearance/fixcards/nodeform-<n>.md. Done check: the member table is complete, the explosion diff reports zero changed bytes, and the residual list is present. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Build the rain beading and wet-body look. Read tmp/freebuff/reports/app-wetness-and-rain.md, colour-bmak-wet-look.md, paint-plans-v2.md section M5 (Wetness_Refl_Fresnel 0.6 not written, no formula), the 9174 surface and weather report, and the wet rows in Working/Appearance/DROPPED_ROWS.md. Operator fact: the reference shows rain beading and the body wet in rain. Find the closest JC3 wetness member of the car paint (the wetness scalars in the CarPaintMM cb2 block, and the global weather coupling) and say which part is driven by JC3 weather, which by a per-block value we write. Write the values the body, glass and wheels need into Builds/bm-RC5-wet, script Tools/scripts/rc5_wet.py (--write, --check); where no formula exists, keep the BmAK scalar 0.6 as the number and label the unit bridge UNKNOWN. Done check: each wetness member read back from the container with its source, and the report separates weather-driven from authored parts. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.
